parameters.content:
## ppwr-intake-check

Where the loop closes. A submission arrives, its documents get read, the engine decides, and the supplier is told what happened.

**In:** `{ campaign_item_id, submission_id }` from 02, or from a replay.

**Order of operations**

1. Load the submission, the item, the campaign and the documents
2. Read each document into fields, keeping the confidence on each
3. Fold those into what the supplier typed, where a typed answer always wins
4. Call 05 and hash the findings it produced
5. Write the findings, update the submission, log the transition
6. Tell the supplier, or tell a reviewer

**The verdict is read off the engine's summary**, not decided here. One implementation of what counts as conform, and it is the one with the tests behind it.

**`evaluated_at` is picked once**, written on the submission, and handed to the engine as its clock. Replay an old submission with its stored value and you get the original verdict back, instead of a two year old declaration being judged against today.

**Article 50 marking is conditional.** A gap notice with a drafted covering paragraph carries the disclosure line and the machine-readable envelope. A confirmation carries neither, because nothing in it was drafted.

Code nodes are built from `src/intake/` by `npm run bundle`.

### Load

Five reads, no writes. Everything the engine sees comes from here.

### Read and decide

Documents to fields, fields to findings. The one model call on this lane cannot change a verdict.

### Record and tell

Findings, then the submission, then the state change, then the supplier. Nothing is sent for a verdict that was not written down first.

nodes.name: Defaults
nodes.notes: Ship-time defaults, overlaid by the meta table. Blank endpoint and notices off out of the box: an operator points this at a real endpoint by writing meta rows, not by editing this workflow.

nodes.name: Load campaign item
nodes.notes: Read from the submission instead of from the request, so a caller that passes a campaign_item_id belonging to a different submission cannot make the two disagree.

nodes.name: Load vendor
nodes.notes: Soft. A missing vendor row must not stop a verdict being recorded; it only means nobody can be told about it, and that failure belongs in the send step.

nodes.name: Load campaign
nodes.notes: Carries the ruleset version the campaign froze at launch, and the hash of the file it froze. Both are checked before anything is evaluated.

nodes.name: Documents to read
nodes.notes:
Built from src/intake/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

Always at least one item. An empty fan-out would leave everything downstream unexecuted and the submission would sit in 'submitted' with no verdict and no error.

nodes.name: Read documents
nodes.notes: Mode is 'each'. One document per execution is what keeps the extraction routes from converging on one node with data on two of them.

value.data: ={{ { doc_type: $json.doc_type, extracted: $json.extracted, extraction_model_id: $json.extraction_model_id, extraction_at: new Date().toISOString() } }}

nodes.name: Record extraction
nodes.notes:
What the model read, and what it decided the document is, on the row of the document it read it from. The classified type is what makes document_present able to pass at all: every upload arrives filed as 'other'.

Mode is 'each'. The store answers one request per call.

nodes.name: Assemble engine input
nodes.notes:
Built from src/intake/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

evaluated_at is chosen here, once, and is both written on the submission and handed to the engine as its clock.

nodes.name: Call rule engine
nodes.notes: Mode is 'once'. One submission, one evaluation. The engine is the only thing in this project allowed to decide anything.

nodes.name: Hash findings
nodes.notes: The reproducibility proof. Re-running this submission with its stored evaluated_at has to produce this hash again, and if it does not, something changed that should not have.

nodes.name: Assess verdict
nodes.notes:
Built from src/intake/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

Reads the verdict off the engine's summary instead of recomputing it from the findings.

nodes.name: Write findings
nodes.notes:
Every finding, including the ones that passed. An auditor asking what was checked deserves the whole list, not the failures.

Mode is 'each'. The store answers one request per call.

nodes.name: Update submission
nodes.notes: Mode is 'each'. The store answers one request per call.

value.transition: ={{ { campaign_item_id: $('Assess verdict').first().json.campaign_item_id, submission_id: $('Assess verdict').first().json.submission_id, from_state: 'submitted', to_state: $('Assess verdict').first().json.verdict, event_type: 'verdict_' + $('Assess verdict').first().json.verdict, actor: 'system', payload: $('Assess verdict').first().json.event_payload } }}

nodes.name: Record verdict transition
nodes.notes:
The item moves and the event is logged in one call, because a state change that is not logged is not a state change.

Mode is 'each'. The store answers one request per call.

nodes.name: Reopen at the failing page
nodes.notes:
The supplier's existing link still works. It reopens where the gap is instead of at the top, and nothing they already answered is lost.

Mode is 'each'. The store answers one request per call.

nodes.name: Build cover request
nodes.notes: Built from src/intake/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

nodes.name: Draft covering paragraph
nodes.notes: The model is shown the finished list and asked to write around it. It cannot add a point, drop one or soften one: the notice builder compares the check identifiers it mentions against the ones in the notice and fails the execution on a mismatch.

nodes.name: Build gap notice
nodes.notes:
Built from src/intake/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

Two inputs, one of which ever carries data: the endpoint's answer, or the request node's own item when no endpoint is configured. The Article 50 marking follows the paragraph instead of the notice.

nodes.name: Build review notice
nodes.notes: Built from src/intake/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

nodes.name: Build confirmation
nodes.notes: Built from src/intake/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

parameters.subject: ={{ 'Review needed: ' + $json.subject }}
parameters.bodyContent: ={{ 'A submission needs a decision before the supplier can be answered.\n\n' + JSON.stringify($('Assess verdict').first().json.event_payload, null, 2) }}

nodes.name: Notify reviewer
nodes.notes: The reviewer gets the indeterminate check identifiers and the counts. The supplier gets a neutral acknowledgement and nothing about what is unresolved, because a supplier told which check is ambiguous is being invited to answer the check instead of the question.

nodes.name: Load settings
nodes.notes:
Soft. A deployment with no meta rows runs on the defaults instead of failing, which is why the first deploy work before anybody has configured anything.

Mode is 'each'. The store answers one request per call.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes:
Built from src/intake/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

Defaults with the meta table laid over them. Every node downstream still reads $('Configuration'), so this is the only place that knows settings can come from anywhere else.

nodes.name: Extraction rows
nodes.notes:
Built from src/intake/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

Accepts the classification against the confidence floor and emits nothing for a document nobody read, which is what stops the store call running on an empty fan-out.
